title_review: Great food and atmosphere, but a little snobby
review_preview: We really enjoyed our meal at Sesamo. It was delicious and lovingly prepared, and nice to receive the dishes from the owner and chef, who was very courteous and also took time to explain each dish on the menu to us. However, the one waiter...
review_full: We really enjoyed our meal at Sesamo. It was delicious and lovingly prepared, and nice to receive the dishes from the owner and chef, who was very courteous and also took time to explain each dish on the menu to us. However, the one waiter working the evening we were there seemed to take a disliking to us from the moment we walked in. We did not have a reservation, and this seemed to annoy said waiter, who meticulously checked the reservations book (there were 3, all already seated) and then had a wander around for 2 or 3 minutes before reluctantly seating us. He didn't offer to get us drinks, and when I asked him, he said "one minute" and walked off and didn't come back. I can only assume he thought we were not big spenders and did not want to give us his attention (there was another big table with whom he was completely enamoured). Luckily, the owner/chef more than made up for the waiter's inadequacy, taking our drinks order, chatting to us and bringing our dishes over. The food itself was great - beautifully presented and delicious veggie tapas. There was a lot of oil and cheese and it certainly was filling! All in all it was a great experience, and we ate until we were bursting (and had wine) for 20 euros each. I don't feel that we could have spent much more as we were totally full, but perhaps the waiter would have liked us to have some cocktails, or the tasting menu at 25€ each. Sorry to have rambled on about the waiter, and don't let it stop you from going here, but I wanted to give an honest review!

review_full: When you go to Spain, do not expect the same quality service as you would in the US. This was true in many of the places we visited on our trip. Especially in Barcelona where many people are downright rude. I have to say, however, that the Restaurante Salamanca is an exception. My husband and I were looking for a place to have paella in the Barceloneta and were redirected here by our cab driver. There was no wait (as we were expecting on a Thursday night) and we were able to pick our own table. The restaurant itself is quite old. And there is not much of a sea view. Initially we received weird looks from the waiters, but I think it had more to do with the fact that we were unsure where to sit. Once seated however, we were treated immediately and were provided excellent service. We did order the paella with lobster. While waiting, they brought out the customary bread with tomato and some chorizo for us to nibble on as an appetizer. Yum to all things we ate! We had decided to splurge this night and it was worth it. When asked if we wanted to order dessert, and we had declined, the waiters still brought out a digestif and some almond cake. The digestif did help and I was able to enjoy some of the dessert. I enjoyed our night out and would go again.

review_full: Our meal at Hoja Santa was a mind blowing experience to say in the least. My husband and I opted for the tasting menu and were so glad we did. Each course was superb, and the menu as a whole was so thoughtful and well planned that we truly felt we were having an immersive dining experience.  One of our favorite courses was none other than the "Trump Taco" which featured delicious pork cut from the suckling pig we had the pleasure of viewing at the beginning of our meal. Democrat or Republican, we can all agree that a strong parallel can be drawn between our president and a steaming pile of swine.  For beverages, we each began our meal with a margarita and shared a bottle of wine for the remainder. The bottle prices were so reasonable we found ourselves doing a double take to ensure we weren't looking at by the glass pricing. The service throughout our meal was also impeccable. Our meal was a Saturday lunch reservation, which I highly recommend if you're having trouble securing a booking. The meal took roughly 2.5 hours and we enjoyed every minute.

I'd advise everyone to take a visit there when they're in Barcelona as I couldn't fault it at all and it was easily the best meal we had!

title_review: Meat in a grand old environment above the city
review_preview: After several days of amazing fish and seafood, and the high energy of the city we wanted something different, meat focused and calm - Asador de Aranda in Tibidabo gave us that.Situated in what was obviously a wealthy neighborhood above the city, the restaurant...
review_full: After several days of amazing fish and seafood, and the high energy of the city we wanted something different, meat focused and calm - Asador de Aranda in Tibidabo gave us that. Situated in what was obviously a wealthy neighborhood above the city, the restaurant is in an old and large villa of architectural merit. The interior is very interesting, but its the outdoor courtyard and terraces that are a wonderful place to dine. The menu is very meat focused, and ALL parts of the animal are used and served - this is not the place for a vegetarian, or someone who might be squeamish about animal heads looking back at them off the plate. The suckling pig and lamb was tremendous, as were the multiple meat based appetizers we tried. They do have English menu's, but the english of the wait staff was limited, which made for some fun moments when attempting to order cocktails. I would say most of the patrons were local/Spanish speakers. As with every restaurant we at at in Barcelona and Sitges, the wait staff were very friendly, yet professional. I would recommend it if you want to get out of the high activity of the city, and you like meat in ALL its forms.

title_review: Cool Venu, Awful Service, Tiny and Overpriced Cocktails
review_preview: Initially I went here due to the great reviews, I always tend to use TripAdvisor when I am abroad to visit some great spots. However on this occasion myself and my partner arrived around 10:45pm to the bar on a Wednesday evening to find a...
review_full: Initially I went here due to the great reviews, I always tend to use TripAdvisor when I am abroad to visit some great spots. However on this occasion myself and my partner arrived around 10:45pm to the bar on a Wednesday evening to find a queue. This was fine, the doorman was incredibly rude but this didn't actually bother me. After around 25 minutes we were let in by a woman who seemed to be a manager/owner, she was wearing a headset to communicate with the doorman, and was showing people to seats etc. This was all fine. The venue itself was really cool and really pretty although the music they played was a bit pop/cheesy at times which didn't suit the vibe - still no issue with that. The issue came when after being shown to our seats and given a menu, having to then wait around 15 minutes to be seen to. I did try and call the woman who showed us to our seats over, and she eventually came and took our order which was fine. If I had of known table service would be this long I would prefer to have gone to the bar, however this is not possible here. Then after around minutes I called her over and said I had been waiting here for ages and still had no drinks, instead of apologising she very rudely retorted with ' we are busy your drinks are being made'. She eventually brings over the drinks and tells me that the time they were put through on the till was only ' 14 minutes ago, so not ages like you said'. Please bear in mind we had to wait around 15 minutes to have our order taken in the first place. When we received the drinks, this is no exaggeration whatsoever, they were half empty.I was so shocked. My boyfriends cup actually felt empty and we could only see ice, to the point where I went over to the Manager and said this is empty, apparently there was a hole in the straw and this was why he couldn't get any liquid out... however that doesn't change the fact we paid 11euro each for a half empty, bang average cocktail, Now don't get me wrong, I am happy to pay 11 euro for cocktails in really nice venues when they are delicious and plentiful, I live in London so I am used to premium prices for this type of thing and dont mind as I was on holiday. However given the shocking rudeness of the Manager, the quality of the cocktail as well as the poor service, half empty drinks and queue just to get in, I really honestly would avoid this place. I am not one to leave reviews usually unless I feel service is exceptional or terrible, and sadly for this place it is the latter. There are much better venues in Barcelona which are less pretentious and have nicer staff, so whilst the venue is undoubtedly cool, sadly its a no from me!

review_full: After having been to Tainos a number of times and having had a party there...always spending quite a lot, this time tonight will be the last time. I went with a friend and we ordered 8 glasses of red wine and various tapas to eat. When the bill came we had been charged per glass. When we had mentioned this earlier to the waitress, she had made a snarky comment about 'you'll know better next time!' We asked if instead we could pay for a bottle as we had obviously consumed one. We were told it was impossible as it 'had gone through the system...' This is a bar, not a multinational! Then my friend was offered a sangría on the house, I did not get one. This, quite frankly, is cheap and very ugly. If you are going to offer something on the house to appease unhappy customers, you offer the whole group not just one member of the group.  When I complained to the waitress, she basically had the attitude of 'well it ain't my bar, so what do you want me to do about it?'. Again, not the best attitude to have. Carrer de Parlament is a busy, vibrant street with high-end eateries and drinking holes. If it were my establishment, I would be trying to court my clientel not pissing them off and driving them into the willing arms of my competition. Small mindedness, and short-sightedness reigns again, unfortunately.  I would recommend trying their comeptitors, who are generally more obliging and welcoming of return custom. What a shame for them!

review_full: Hello, Tonight myself and my partner visited your skybar in Grand Central Hotel Barcelona. We had great service from the man on reception who could not have done more for us. When we went up to the skybar we were greeted by staff and seated at the very back corner away from all other guests. We were served our first drink which was the €16 charge that all skybar guests have if not staying in the hotel.  After this we sat for over an hour with empty drinks and staff who looked over at us multiple times but did not try to serve us.  A member of staff then approached the table of young girls next to us & proceeded to chat & flirt for over 10 minutes with them, we tried to engage with the member of staff to order another drink and were ignored again.  After this we decided to leave so tried to speak to staff to pay and were yet again ignored. We then thought that we were to pay at the hotel reception and so went to the lift where staff shouted after us.  We paid €32 and discussed with the member of staff what had happened with their staff. He did not seem to care at all and allowed us to leave extremely unhappy.  This ruined our night & as guests from Scotland we are disappointed that one of our last nights on holiday has been ruined.  We loved the view and ambience at the Skybar & would of highly recommended it to fellow visitors to Barcelona however as a result of this experience with staff we will be highly recommending not to visit. We would not like our friends/family to be treated the way we were & still expected to pay the full charge despite the full charge.

I wish we had more time in Barcelona so we could have eaten there again. Next visit, I will book a hotel close to this place just so we can go more than once.

review_full: I was there last week with 7 colleagues from work. At La Taina you can order a predefined menu that consists in a lot of food including appetisers, main course, desserts, coffee, wine and water (all 25 euros). We thought it was a good deal if you were hungry. We planned to ask 6 'predefined menus' and an extra main course since one of us was not very hungry because she was not feeling good. They did not let us do that, everybody should go either for the predefined menu or order individually 7 main courses. Also, we asked if we could change a bottle of wine by water and they did not let us do that neither. So, we ended up ordering 7 predefined menus, some extra water and an extra main course. Interestingly, when the waitress brought us the last appetiser said : ok, now, eat until you explode! Quite rude, isn't it? Of course, we could not finish all the food and almost none of us ate desserts and coffee.  When we paid, they rounded up each part without asking .  So, despite they gave us a lot of food, the quality of the food did not worth 25 euros. The staff was not very nice, actually, I would say they were rude. Also, it was a noisy restaurant. I would not recommend it to my friends.

When we were given the menu, there was no "menu of the day" listed so I asked, and the very abrupt waiter said that it was only available during the week. We reconciled to order pasta from the regular menu, and it was fine; but, as we were eating a large family of about 8 walked in and were seated next to us. When it was time for the to order, they were also refused the "menu of the day" and had to order from the regular menu. Seems like a pattern!! When we left, indeed, the menu was out side the door, and in small print is said Monday through Friday. The strange thing is that the only thing this free-standing sign advertised was the "menu of the day." This is a very dishonest place! Beware! read the fine print! They are sneaky! We do not recommend this restuarant!

The meal was 25€ each with 2 drinks. The food overall was ok but not exceptional and really more like tapas than a Tasting Menu. The service by the chef himself was really friendly and upbeat, but the main waiter was a little glum and not very engaging, which disappointed us. The restaurant is cosy and was full of mainly English speaking customers, who I guess have found this place (like us) via Tripadvisor!

review_preview: I've been to Barcelona so many times and La Fianna (close to Santa Maria del Mar church) is still one of my top places that i visit. www.lafianna.comFrom the moment you enter it is obvious that it is a special place, the atmosphere is...
review_full: I've been to Barcelona so many times and La Fianna (close to Santa Maria del Mar church) is still one of my top places that i visit.  www.lafianna.com From the moment you enter it is obvious that it is a special place, the atmosphere is great, nice music, lights shine just enough not to interfere with the hedonism in the air- the first part of the space you enter is a nice bar, and when you enter further inside, on your left there is the jewel of the house- the right place for you if you are for a good meal- Greece-like pedestals and curtained beds filled with cushions- the food is not served as you would expect from a restaurant, it is served like it should be served in an ambient like Fianna's, you will get it on a big feast plate like the golden ones you have seen on the movies about emperors that ruled some 2000 years ago. And the food is great, let me tell you that, you can check the prices on their web site, I tried the duck and it was delicious. There is a good selection of wine also, good priced. The thing that gives the biggest part to the ambient are the two more than 400 years old chandeliers hanging from the ceiling above your head, you will definitely love those. There is a queue for this relaxation zone for those who would like to drink and not to eat, a rope discretely separates the bar from the restaurant "hedonism" part, and if you pick a spot you would like to lie on, but you don't have a reservation it might take some time before it becomes available. but if you would like to eat, don't stand in the queue, tell the nice staff that you are there to eat and you will get your seat more quickly. La Fianna is a great atmosphere, and value for money place, a great one to enter for a good night with your friends/one you love/colleague, either you are there just for a drink or you would like to eat. It is open late, and the neighborhood it is situated in is a nice one for finding more special places after you finish with La Fianna.

review_preview: We ended up by accident in Rossini at 10pm on a November Friday because our booked restaurant (Café de l’Academia) had suffered a power cut and was closed. We decided we’d look for a pizza instead and rambled until we came across this place under...
review_full: We ended up by accident in Rossini at 10pm on a November Friday because our booked restaurant (Café de l’Academia) had suffered a power cut and was closed. We decided we’d look for a pizza instead and rambled until we came across this place under the arcade on Plaza Real. We sat outside as it was a balmy night (at least by Irish standards) and ordered 2 ”tapas” portions of calamari (€4.50), followed by 2 pizzas (€13-15). The calamari was very tasty and came as a good sized portion - but the pizzas were enormous and generously topped. My wife could only finish half hers – after a struggle, while I left about a third of mine behind. Both were very good but just too big for us. I noticed that we were not alone among the diners in being unable to eat the lot.  We had a nice bottle of Ribero del Duero (€37), probably a little overpriced. Service was efficient and friendly – the waiter laughed when we had to abandon the effort and suggested that next time we might share a pizza and a salad. Good advice. We had no room for dessert and finished with a couple of ok coffees. The menu had many options other than pizza and the ambience was quite lively. It’s nice to sit outside under the arcade and watch the varied nightlife go by. When we left at about 11.30pm, the locals were still coming in to dine. I'll never fathom how the Spanish/Catalans can eat so late at night.

review_full: This got a good write up in the local paper so we thought it was time to try it out. Alas it wasn't very busy (it was Thursday evening of the puente) so the atmosphere suffered a little, but the quality of the food, wine and service made up for it.  One of the great things about this place is they do "media racion" which means half plate. So if you want to sample a number of small dishes you can, and still have room for dessert. The restaurant has a great selection of wines. Brunus is always a favorite and all good restaurants have it on the wine list. The last time I was in the US I had a taste of kobe beef, incredibly expensive, specially prepared Japanese style. At Agut I had a "solomillo de buey". It was equally as good. Cooked to perfection, sliced like butter, melted in the mouth. It's been a while since I had such a great piece of beef for less than 25Eu, (and 1/5th of what the kobe cost!). If you ever decide you want a little bit of traditional Catalan cuisine (not tapas), there are a ton of great restaurants to chose from. This is one of the best value for money.

Finally, we gave up and just waited for whatever would come... The hake was undercooked, but the cod was well prepared. The salads were poor and not what we tried to order (we do have a fluent Spanish speaker in the group). The dessert has an assortment of 6 dishes, but not sure if that was one order or two. They ranged from good to poor. The wine list was reasonably prices and had good variety. If I had written this the next day, perhaps 4 star, but after meals at PLA and Arcaro, 3 is on target.

review_full: My wife and I and another couple visited this restaurant last year and loved it – so as we were all passing through Barcelona in July we decided to visit again. We were warmly welcomed, particularly when they found out that we’d come all the way from Australia because we loved their food. Perhaps a slight exaggeration on our part, but we did enjoy our last visit.  The ambiance was similar to last year, although we did notice that the restaurant had some alterations, but these alteration didn’t affect where we sat.  After the meal we were asked by our male waiter what we thought of the food this year, and did we have any suggestions.  We did – our meals were warm at best, and we suggested that they serve the ready dishes as quickly as possible, and not wait for all four meals to be ready (which what happened, making all but one meal warm to cold). We also commented that we didn’t think the meal was as good as last year, and then we found out they had a different chef. Perhaps our memories were at fault, and we remembered last year through rose coloured glasses, but there no getting away that our dishes were cold to warm. Our next visit to Barcelona may or may not include this restaurant.

review_full: We turned up to Llamber around 8.10pm on our final night in Barcelona and thought we would try our luck for a table. We were told that a table was 30 minutes away and to come back at 8.40pm. The manager warned us if we were not back by 8.40pm they would give away the table - fair enough.  We came back at 8.40pm and were told a table was "2 minutes" away. 15 minutes later there was still no table so we asked if there would be one available soon - as from what we could see it didn't look like any were coming up. We were told that no, they were just getting the bill for a table and that they wouldn't be long so we should order a drink while we wait. We ordered 4 glasses of wine which we drank on the side of the street. By 9.15pm we still had no table so I went inside to pay for the drinks and leave. The manger again told me that the table was '2 minutes away' and that they were just paying the bill. I told him that we had been told this 40 minutes ago. He got a bit angry and upset that we were leaving - probably because he knew he knew he had mislead us.  I completely understand that these things happen sometimes. However, no apology was attempted to be made at any stage nor did they try and make us more comfortable at all. We spent over an hour of our evening messing around with this place due to bad communication. From other reviews the food sounds amazing but my experience was quite the opposite and completely disappointing

My partner ended up ordering a leek and potato soup kind of dish which was lukewarm at best, and I ordered some coca bread which was literally dry toast. For our mains, my partner ordered beef medallions "medium-rare" well they came rare, practically still with a heartbeat! I ordered steak well done and it came absolutely swimming in blood, had to send it back. Once my meal returned my partner had already nearly finished, so it was disappointing we weren't able to enjoy our meal together.  We ordered puddings and to be fair they weren't so bad. All in all, I would probably recommend trying another restaurant at Las Arenas as this really wasn't all that great.

It almost feels like each dish was small so that you’d slow and appreciate each bite, yet just enough that you don’t get bored of any one dish/taste. We were tempted to order the same thing twice, but we’re glad we didn’t, because everything was special and unique. I’m not sure if the menu changes often, but my recommendations would be to try the stuffed squid, the hake roe, any of the mollettes, and definitely the jamon. I’ve also heard they specialize in vermouth but I didn’t get to try that.  The price is ridiculously affordable too: for 2 people over lunch (without alcohol), it was about 60 euros, which is a steal when you taste the amazing food. Would 100% come back!

title_review: Not the greatest place for Vegetarians, but overall quite pleasant.
review_preview: I recently went to Santa Gula for the first time with a big group for a birthday party.  It's a very tastefully decorated place in a beautiful location, very attractive both for a small group or even a table as big as ours.  It is...
review_full: I recently went to Santa Gula for the first time with a big group for a birthday party. It's a very tastefully decorated place in a beautiful location, very attractive both for a small group or even a table as big as ours. It is not spacious, so you will be sitting quite close to the other diners, but the overall atmosphere is quite nice and the service exceptional.  Our group was composed of about 15 people and four of us were vegetarians. They divided up the table so people could share according to eating habits, which I found to be a professional decision. The food that was brought out as starters, a variety of small dishes to share, was fairly tasty. Delicious little cherry tomatoes dressed simply in olive oil, asparagus tempura, a dish of very good bravas, bread, and so on.  However, the main dishes, of which there were two, left much to be desired for those of us that didn't eat meat. The first main was a pasta without sauce, just a small amount of olive oil, with roasted vegetables. The dish was correctly served and cooked, but simply lacked taste. The second main was a dish of sautéed mushrooms, which was tastier than the pasta but, to me, is something that I would serve alongside something more filling. The rest of the diners were served two dishes that were quite a bit more developed and everyone seemed quite pleased. Dessert was a delicious crema catalana/creme brûlée and the wine served throughout the meal was very nice. All for roughly 30€; quite affordable given the location and quality of the meal. Overall, the experience was a very good one-- good food, excellent, attentive service, and a nice location. Perhaps ordering à la carte would reveal some more exciting vegetable based dishes, so I do hope to repeat.

My wife's salad had tomatoes that we so not ripe, that they were green! And the cured meats were dry, rubbery, and fatty, as if it was left over from the day before. I waited nearly 30 minutes before my steak came, and I told the waitress that brought it, that it was very late for the meal. She just looked at me and walked away. By that time, I lost my appetite, but was going to eat it anyways. When I bit into it, it was chewy and dried out meat. The local at the table next to me had the same dish and complained as well. The worst part was the female waitress though! When I called her over to complain about it, she gave me the worst look and she got upset with me! That made me upset, so I told her that I didn't want it and it was not cooked right and I didn't want to pay for it. She basically grabbed my dish, then brought the bill over and basically threw it at me. I never complain about restaurants, as you can see by my past posts, but this place needs to be written up. If she handled the situation differently, I would have been ok with just the bad food, but this truly goes down as one very bad experience.

review_preview: This place is cool, chic, modern, groovy and a fantastic find.It's intimate and because its so so good, expect it to be busy. It's a great vibe though! We hadn't booked but were greeted nicely on entry, asked if we would like to wait...
review_full: This place is cool, chic, modern, groovy and a fantastic find. It's intimate and because its so so good, expect it to be busy. It's a great vibe though! We hadn't booked but were greeted nicely on entry, asked if we would like to wait 1/2 an hour and enjoy a drink at the bar and we are so glad we did. We were seated at the bar after about 10 mins and we ordered around 5 mins later and food started coming out 5 - 10 mins after that. Very organized and attentive service. It's not cheap, it's not expensive, you do pay pay for the superb quality but the servings are generous. The flavours were outstanding. The food has a modern and sometimes unique twist. Every dish we ordered was simply amazing and we love good food. We had the beef skewer which had very lean succulent meat, the duck Caesar salad and the fried egg with the ham and chips ( homemade lightly fried crisps and delicious Iberian ham) and the chicken croquettes. Now for a lighter, feeling content stomach we could have stopped here, but as the food was so tasty and it was our last night we ordered another two glasses of Chardonnay, the aubergine fritters with apple, goats cheese and honey and the Mc Pepita which is their take on a tapas style burger which we shared and highly recommend.... I'd eat these all day long! Two of us, 6 dishes and two glasses of Chardonnay for just over 50 euro. We would happily go earlier and spend a 100 and try more but we simply didn't have time. This topped any Tapas styled food we found in Barcelona and we found two other amazing places whilst we were exploring.

review_preview: We were enjoying a couple of days in Barcelona prior to attending a conference and found this charming little restaurant by accident.The few outside tables were already taken as were most the those inside but, being just two of us, we were found a...
review_full: We were enjoying a couple of days in Barcelona prior to attending a conference and found this charming little restaurant by accident. The few outside tables were already taken as were most the those inside but, being just two of us, we were found a quiet table in the bar area. It would appear that we were lucky as during our visit umpteen groups of all sizes were apologetically declined service as the place was at capacity - 2 couples ate at the bar using stools such was the demand. Whilst some of those eating (or being turned away) were likely first time visitors, it seemed that a number of them were also were locals and/or return visitors which perhaps suggests something. Our own lack of experience of eating out in Spain means that there was some slight puzzlement in terms of what we should order and when it would arrive but that aside we found the meal to be truly superb. The meal, ambience, and setting were all memorable BUT were bested by the staff/owners. I have never seen a team continuously work so hard to attend to the needs of their clientele. Only once was my glass left empty for more than a minute before being refilled with another beer. Whilst other staff were obviously on site, there were three young male staff that seemed to not stop all evening. As I stated to one - if they are not the owners, they should be. Overall a truly great experience.
